cards.text: Ezekiel the priest is living among the exiles by the River Chebar (Ezekiel 1:1-3), and the word of the LORD comes to him. God asks what the people mean by quoting this proverb about the land of Israel: 'The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the teeth of the children are set on edge.' Hold on. Dad eats the sour grapes, and the KIDS are the ones making the face?

cards.question: The people of Israel keep quoting that sour grapes proverb. What is it really saying?

answers.text: Children pay for their fathers' sins
Children turn out like their fathers
Fathers pay for their children's sins

cards.text: And God is not having it. 'As surely as I live, declares the Lord GOD, you will no longer quote this proverb in Israel.'

cards.question: Before God settles the sour grapes question, He says every soul belongs to someone. Who?
Every soul, father and son, belongs to God. So in God's eyes, whose sin does a soul die for?

cards.text: God puts it plain: 'The soul who sins is the one who will die.' That sour grapes proverb just got shoved to the back of the junk drawer, and believe me, friend, I KNOW how dark it gets back there.

Now God walks through one family. First, suppose a man is righteous: he doesn't eat at the mountain or look to idols, doesn't defile his neighbor's wife, doesn't oppress anyone, doesn't rob and doesn't take excess interest.

cards.question: This righteous man doesn't rob anybody. Instead, he gives his ___ to the hungry and covers the naked with clothing.
This righteous man follows God's statutes and faithfully keeps His ordinances. True or false: God says he will surely live.

cards.text: Now suppose that righteous man has a violent son who sheds blood. Same kitchen, COMPLETELY different batch: this son eats at the mountain, robs, oppresses the poor and needy and lifts his eyes to idols.

cards.question: True or false: Because his father was righteous, the violent son will live.

cards.text: God answers His own question: 'Will this son live? He will not!' Now that violent man has a son of his own, and that son has a front-row seat to every sin his father commits.

cards.question: The violent man's son sees all the sins his father commits. What does he do with what he sees?

answers.text: Thinks it over and does not copy it
Copies his father one sin at a time
Tries to make up for it with offerings

cards.text: So this son stays away from idols, doesn't rob, feeds the hungry and keeps God's ordinances, and God says he will surely live. Took me YEARS in a junk drawer to stop moping, and this man breaks his dad's pattern just by paying attention.

cards.question: And the violent father, who robbed his brother and practiced extortion? God says he will die for his ___ iniquity.

cards.text: Then God says the people may ask, 'Why shouldn’t the son bear the iniquity of his father?' Friend, that's like asking why you didn't get the parking ticket for somebody else's car.

cards.question: Why does God say the son who didn't copy his violent father will surely live?

answers.text: He did what is just and right

cards.text: Then God says it again: 'The soul who sins is the one who will die.' Same words as before, and this time He spells out exactly who doesn't carry whose load.

cards.question: God says a son will not bear the iniquity of his ___, and a father will not bear the iniquity of his ___.

cards.text: God finishes the thought: 'The righteousness of the righteous man will fall upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked man will fall upon him.' Everybody bakes their OWN batch.
Now God flips it around. Suppose a wicked man turns from all the sins he has committed, keeps all God's statutes and does what is just and right.

cards.question: True or false: A wicked man who turns from all his sins and does what is just and right will still die for the sins he committed before.

cards.text: None of the transgressions he committed will be held against him. NOBODY is digging his old receipts out of the junk drawer.

cards.question: Then God asks whether He takes any pleasure in the death of the wicked. What would He prefer for the wicked man?

answers.text: That he turns from his ways and lives
That he pays for every one of his sins
That he stays far away from Israel

cards.text: But it works the other way too. Suppose a righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits the same abominations as the wicked.

cards.question: A righteous man turns away and starts doing what the wicked do. What happens to all the righteous acts he did before?

answers.text: None of them will be remembered
They cancel out his new sins
They protect his children from harm

cards.text: Because of his unfaithfulness and sin, he will die. You can't coast on last year's batch, friend.

cards.question: The people answer back, 'The way of the Lord is not just.' True or false: God turns it around and says it's Israel's ways that are unjust.

cards.text: So God lays it out again. The righteous man who turns to iniquity will die for it, and the wicked man who turns to what is just and right will save his life.

cards.question: True or false: The wicked man lives because he considered and turned from all the transgressions he had committed.

cards.text: And the house of Israel says it again: 'The way of the Lord is not just.' God answers them again too, and I'm telling you, that's hitting snooze and expecting the alarm to give up.

cards.question: Then God tells the house of Israel how He will judge them. How?

answers.text: By the sins of their fathers

cards.question: God calls out to the house of Israel: Repent and ___ from all your transgressions, so that your iniquity will not become your downfall.

cards.text: Then God tells them to cast away all the transgressions they've committed. Not tuck them in a drawer for later. Cast them AWAY.

cards.question: Along with casting away their transgressions, God tells the house of Israel to fashion for themselves a new ___ and a new ___.

cards.text: Then God asks, 'Why should you die, O house of Israel?' I don't hear a judge banging a gavel there, friend. I hear somebody leaving the porch light on.

cards.question: True or false: God says He takes pleasure in the death of anyone who won't repent.

cards.text: The passage ends with God's call: 'So repent and live!' That's not a threat, friend, that's an INVITATION, and believe me, an invitation got ME out of a junk drawer.
